🚨🇲🇽 <u>After 12 Dead at Mazatlán's El Castillo Prison, the Federal Government Will Build a New One</u>

Security chief Omar García Harfuch announced a new federally funded penitentiary in Sinaloa, ordered by President Sheinbaum, after deadly violence inside the El Castillo prison in Mazatlán. "The Government of Mexico will build, with federal resources, a new penitentiary center in Sinaloa, modern, safe and with the necessary infrastructure to strengthen penitentiary control," he said. Meanwhile, El Castillo has been reinforced with National Guard and federal prison staff. Governor Graciela Domínguez is providing the land.
banner: SINALOA: NEW FEDERAL PRISON AFTER 12 DEAD

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Fobaproa's Real Beneficiaries: PRI Insiders, Tycoons and Bankers</u>

A new Contralínea investigation names who Zedillo's bank bailout actually rescued: Claudio X. González Laporte, Agustín F. Legorreta, Carlos Cabal Peniche, Jorge Lankenau and others. Even the PRI itself had set up four trusts at Banco Unión and Banca Cremi before the December 1994 crash. The bill never closes: 552 billion pesos recognized in 1998 have already cost 1.6 trillion in interest alone, with the principal still growing. Next year's payment, 48 billion pesos, is roughly twice the entire budget of Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro. Every Fobaproa IOU was signed without the congressional approval Article 73 of the Constitution requires.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>First Stop of the Health Tour: Sheinbaum in Eastern Edomex, 98% Medicine Supply</u>

A day after announcing she would personally inspect IMSS-Bienestar hospitals in every state in the system, Sheinbaum was in eastern Estado de México with Governor Delfina Gómez, urging people to use the public system and highlighting 98% medicine supply. On the table in Texcoco: Hospital Valle Ceylán in Tlalnepantla, the Atenco General Hospital, and a new oncology wing at the Ixtapaluca high-specialty hospital. Free care for people with no social security, checked hospital by hospital.

🇲🇽🌀 <u>Hurricane Simon: Army Puts 2,895 Troops in Place Before Landfall</u>

Before Simon even touched land, Mexico's Defense Ministry had 2,895 soldiers, National Guard and Air Force personnel deployed across Nayarit, Colima and Jalisco under Plan DN-III-E. Behind them: a 300-strong regional task force in Zapopan, heavy machinery staged in Puerto Vallarta and Tepic, 11 aircraft, plus engineering, health, supply and communications teams. Simon reached Category 4. The state was already there.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Peso Falls 9% in Five Weeks as the Fed Hikes and Banxico Weighs Cuts</u>

The peso closed Friday at 18.4111 per dollar, its fifth straight weekly loss, according to El Economista. It has lost 1.52 pesos since September 4, when it traded at 16.8912. The trigger was the gap between the two central banks: the Fed raised rates, while minutes released Thursday showed three of Banxico's five board members open to cutting from 6.5%, which shrinks the carry-trade premium.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Tlaxcala: 40 Human Trafficking Convictions and 1,106 Years in Prison</u>

Sheinbaum highlighted the federal government's coordination with Governor Lorena Cuéllar against human trafficking in Tlaxcala, a state that for decades was synonymous with trafficking networks. The state prosecutor's office reports 40 convictions from 2022 to September 2026, totaling 1,106 years in prison: one in 2022, five in 2023, 16 in 2024, 10 in 2025 and eight so far this year. Health inspectors have also shut down nine motels in the "Mujeres Libres de Violencia" operation.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>Hurricane Simon Knocks Out Power to 65,000 in Guerrero; CFE Restores 90.5% by Dawn</u>

The Puerto Marqués substation flooded at 3:54 p.m. on October 8 and had to be shut down. By 5 a.m. the next day, CFE director Emilia Calleja reported power back for 90.5% of the 65,078 affected users across 13 municipalities, from Acapulco to the Costa Chica. The 6,135 still without service were mostly in San Luis Acatlán, where crews were using heavy machinery to clear landslides.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>The Chihuahua Security Chief Who Opened His Tower to US Agencies Now Runs the State Prosecutor's Office</u>

Governor Maru Campos has named Gilberto Loya, her public security secretary, acting head of the Chihuahua State Attorney General's Office. In April, after CIA agents turned up in a state operation, Loya said the Torre Centinela was open for the "eventual and, eventually, permanent presence" of foreign agencies. Sheinbaum said then that only the state prosecutor's office or Loya's own security ministry could have made deals with the CIA, and the FGR opened an investigation. Now Loya heads one of those two offices.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>UNCTAD: Mexico Exports Booming, Development Lagging</u>

Manufactures have made up more than 80% of Mexico's exports since the mid-1990s, led by autos, electronics and IT. A new UN Conference on Trade and Development report says the boom never built a domestic base: in electronics, 70.7% of the gross value Mexico exports is foreign components. Thirty years of NAFTA-era integration left Mexico as, in large part, an assembly platform.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Diesel Tax Stays at Zero for a Fifth Week; Gasoline Relief Increased</u>

With Brent rising on Strait of Hormuz threats and Hurricane Isaías shutting in 1.3 million barrels a day in the Gulf, Mexico's Treasury kept the 100% IEPS tax break on diesel for October 10-16 and raised relief on gasoline, El Economista reports. Magna now gets 4.31 pesos per liter off (64%), and Premium gets 4.03 pesos (71%). Drivers pay 2.39 pesos of IEPS tax per liter on Magna and zero on diesel. National averages: Magna 23.70, diesel 27.00 pesos per liter. Oil shocks abroad are absorbed by the state, not passed to the pump.
banner: DIESEL TAX AT ZERO, 5TH WEEK RUNNING
